intro.author: Paul, with Timothy named as co-sender (1:1). Traditionally accepted as Paul's; some modern scholars think a follower wrote it in his name.
intro.written: If by Paul, about AD 60–62, while he was in prison (4:3, 18), traditionally in Rome
intro.audience: Believers at Colossae, a small town in the Lycus valley of Asia Minor, near Laodicea and Hierapolis
intro.setting: Paul had never visited Colossae (2:1); the church was founded by Epaphras, a local believer who had worked with Paul (1:7; 4:12). Teachers there were urging extra practices on the believers: special knowledge, food and festival rules, harsh self-denial and the 'worshipping of angels' (2:16-23). The exact nature of this teaching is debated. Tychicus and Onesimus carried the letter (4:7-9).
intro.purpose: Paul shows that Christ is supreme over all things and fully sufficient, so believers need nothing added to him, and describes the new life that flows from belonging to him.
intro.bigIdea: Christ is supreme over all creation, and in him believers are complete.

outline.title: Complete in Christ, not in human rules

commentary.t: THE EPISTLE OF PAUL THE APOSTLE TO THE COLOSSIANS
